title: Transient KV-slicing, compressed prefetch shepherd and model-hedge lifecycle for graceful OOM recovery
creator: Daniel Ruiz
description: Problem: Periodic OOM events on high-concurrency inference pools are primarily caused by unbounded KV working sets and aggressive continuous-batching spikes. Current mitigations (eviction thresholds and naive prefetch disable) cause hard failures or large latency regressions. Goal: introduce a safety-net architecture that (1) keeps memory usage under control with minimal quality loss, (2) allows fast recovery via retries and hedged fallbacks to smaller model lanes, and (3) is observable and tunable from the Console.
proposal_summary: Implement a three-part system: (A) transient KV-slicing with lossy compression for low-priority prefixes; (B) a prefetch shepherd that stagers prefetch work and can reduce or defer prefetch based on headroom predictions; (C) a model-hedge lifecycle that attempts a short retry with reduced batch/admission from the same model, then routes to a compact quantized variant or micro-model on sustained pressure. Include circuit-breakers, safe admission controller, and progressive fidelity tiers so callers see graceful degradation rather than abrupt failures.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use lightweight lossy compression (fast int8 delta compression) for cold KV slices to save memory at modest reconstruction cost; tradeoff is CPU spend on decompress vs GPU OOM avoidance.
Prefetch shepherd delays non-critical prefetches under predicted spikes instead of canceling all prefetches, minimizing cold-start latency while protecting headroom.
Fallback to quantized model variants preserves response correctness in most cases; worst-case hallucination risk is acceptable for P0 customer-facing throughput SLOs but tracked via quality monitors.
Hedged retries (short exponential backoff + lower admission) reduce false positive fallback routing but increase request tail latency slightly; acceptable for services prioritizing availability.
We avoid global KV truncation because it causes user-visible context loss; prefer per-request slice degradation with recorded delta so rollups can reconcile.
Implementation complexity increases scheduler CPU usage; we plan staged rollout with conservative thresholds and can disable adaptive features via runtime flags.
Telemetry will include per-request fidelity tag to enable downstream quality regression analysis; cost of tagging is minimal compared to observability gains.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce OOM termination rate in canary pool by >= 90% under synthetic burst tests compared to baseline (same workload).
P99 latency increase for successful requests remains <= 20% versus baseline for steady-state traffic; spikes can experience up to 50% temporary degradation but recover within 30s.
Fallback routing path must succeed for >= 99% of hedged requests without user-visible error (status 200 with fidelity tag).
Prefetch shepherd must lower prefetch queue length under predicted headroom < 10% remaining and avoid increasing cold-start misses by more than 15% at steady state.
All new telemetry (fidelity_tag, eviction_reason, fallback_path, prefetch_deferral_count) are emitted and available in Console dashboards within retention window.
Feature flags and runtime knobs exist to disable compression or hedging per-customer pool without code deploy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (internal canary): add per-request fidelity tag and basic admission controller that enforces headroom budget and emits eviction_reason. Add lightweight KV-slice metadata to track lossy-storage candidates.
Phase 2 (prefetch shepherd): implement prefetch queueing with predictive headroom model (moving-window occupancy predictor) and controller that defers or reorders prefetch tasks.

Phase 3 (compression): integrate fast lossy compression codec for cold KV slices with fallback to full reconstruction if reconstruction fails; instrumentation to measure CPU cost and decompression latency.

Phase 4 (model-hedge lifecycle): implement hedged retry orchestration: initial short retry lowering batch/admission, on continued pressure route to quantized-compact variant or micro-model with preserved API compatibility.
Phase 5 (observability + rollout): add Console views, dashboards, alerts for OOM-class events and fidelity regressions; staged rollout to Dedicated pools and opt-in for Private customers.
Phase 6: run chaos/soak tests and customer canaries, iterate thresholds based on telemetry.
test_plan_and_benchmarks: Synthetic burst tests: 50k concurrent short chats with long contexts to exercise KV pressure. Measure OOM rate, tail latency, and fallback rate.
Cost benchmark: measure average CPU and token costs with compression enabled vs baseline across representative workloads.
Quality checks: run eval prompt set against primary model vs fallback quantized variant to measure delta in ROUGE/embedding-similarity; set alert thresholds.
Soak: 72-hour steady-state load with intermittent spikes to validate long-tail stability and memory oscillation damping.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alert 'oom-safety-net-triggered' when eviction_reason == 'safety_net' fires > 5/min for 5m in a pool.
Dashboard tile: headroom_prediction vs actual occupancy with annotations for prefetch_deferrals and fallback_routing events.
Quality regression alert: fidelity_fallback_delta_alert when averaged metric degrades beyond threshold for 1h.
SLO guard: if fallback_rate > 5% for a production pool continuously for 15m, auto-escalation to SRE and feature-flag disablement.
rollout_and_migration_notes: Default-off for all existing pools; enable via Console toggles per-pool for canary first.
For Dedicated/private customers with strict QoS, provide option to only enable prefetch shepherd and admission controller but keep compression and hedging disabled.
Migration path for existing KV metadata: background job to mark cold prefixes as compressible; safe to roll back because compressed slices are optional and recoverable.
Provide a 'fidelity-preview' header for SDKs so clients can opt-in to receive fidelity hints in responses for analytics.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: compression CPU overhead increases cost. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and CPU budget cap; measure in Phase 3 and throttle compression when CPU budget exceeded.
Risk: fallback model produces quality regressions. Mitigation: strict eval gating, canary the fallback with production traffic shadowing and automatic rollback if regression crosses threshold.
Risk: hedged retry increases tail latency. Mitigation: tune short backoff windows and use admission reduction to keep retry cheap; monitor tail and tune.
Risk: observability blind spots. Mitigation: require emission of fidelity tags and ensure Console ingestion paths are verified in Phase 1.
open_questions: What is the acceptable upper bound for fallback rate per-customer before we auto-disable hedging? (suggested 5%)
Should compressed cold slices be stored on host memory or ephemeral SSD when host memory is also constrained? SSD adds IO latency but may be necessary under extreme pressure.
Do we need a customer-facing SLA note for 'fidelity-tier degradation' when hedging is enabled? Legal/PM input needed.
Which quantized model family should be our first fallback standard for 7B/13B and 70B families? Ops input required.
